item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-08-26

Generated: 2026-08-26 00:00 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project AI Infrastructure Comparison Report — 2026-08-26

1. Ecosystem Overview

The inference stack is consolidating around three battlegrounds: speculative decoding (MTP/EAGLE/DFlash/DSpark) is now table-stakes across every engine but remains the top source of correctness and integration bugs; multi-vendor hardware enablement (AMD ROCm/gfx942, Intel SYCL, Apple MLX/ARM, Qualcomm Hexagon) is driving most new-kernel activity as NVIDIA-only paths no longer suffice; and long-context stability has emerged as the sharpest operational risk — Kimi-K3 engine-wide degeneration appears in both vLLM (#51039) and SGLang (#34815). Quantization formats are proliferating (MXFP4, NVFP4, Q2_0 ternary, EXL3 fractional-bit), but today's digest shows the bleeding edge is still dangerous: vLLM reverted MXFP4+block-FP8 after H100 correctness failures, and Ollama ships a CUDA build that silently drops RTX 30-series GPUs. No project shipped a stable production release in the last 24h except llama.cpp (v0.3.0) and Unsloth (two betas); the rest are mid-transition (vLLM MRV2, Ollama Qwen3.8 fixes, LiteLLM cost-accounting rework).

2. Activity Comparison

Counts below reflect notable issues/PRs referenced in today's digests, not absolute GitHub totals. Severity and release status are from the digests directly.

Project Notable Issues Notable PRs Release Status (24h)
vLLM ~10 open (top: scheduler admission stall #53130, Kimi-K3 degeneration #51039, multi-node gloo deadlock #52907) ~15 (MRV2 default rollout #53183, spec-decode overhead #53694, K2-Horizon #53806) None. MRV2 default transition pending; 1 revert (MXFP4 Humming)
SGLang ~11 open (top: DSV4-Flash EP crashes on Hopper #35557, Kimi-K3 ~30s TTFT floor #34815, DFLASH unsupported under PD #36140) ~16 (AMD MXFP8 MoRI dispatch #36119, Spark3 #35963, expert-choice fusion #29718) None. No new version tagged
llama.cpp ~7 open (top: HIP cross-request leakage #25992, gfx1151 corruption #27579, MTP acceptance collapse #27572) ~14 (KleidiAI rework #26077, Pascal CUDA graphs #27721, SYCL TILE KV #26689) ✅ v0.3.0 released (+ build/KleidiAI/Metal fixes)
Ollama ~16 open (top: DeepSeek-v4-flash cloud thinking loop #17892, Qwen3.8 tool-loop 500 #17778, CUDA 13 drops sm_86 #17841) ~12 (cached prompt tokens #17943, Metal load-time fix #17998, llama.cpp b10630 bump #18003) None. 2 upstream bumps in review; Qwen3.8 regressions live
LiteLLM ~11 open (top: Python 3.10 incompatibility #38202, false BudgetExceededError #36926, Redis ssl_check_hostname #34614) ~13 (cache-read price tie-break #38164, Bedrock GPT-5.x reasoning_effort #38279, Agent 365 MCP guardrail #38241) None. 5 stale issues closed; 5 likely-fixed items closed
Unsloth ~14 open (top: batched vs. single greedy divergence #9708, GGUF tools no-op #9730, auto-compaction fixed threshold #9671) ~10 (EXL3 quant backend #7115, MLX real context length #8125, Qwen3.5 MTP finetune loss #6557) ✅ v0.1.802-beta, v0.1.803-beta (170+ PRs combined)

Signal: vLLM and SGLang are running hot on both bugs and feature PRs; llama.cpp and Unsloth are the only projects shipping tagged releases today.

3. Model Support Race

Project New Model / Architecture Support (24h)
vLLM K2-Horizon (new arch, #53806); Idefics3/SmolVLM full ViT CUDA-graph support (#47625); Kimi-K3 low-latency decode GEMM on SM100/B200 (#53534); EAGLE3/dflash/dspark draft models with pipeline parallelism (#50514)
SGLang Spark3 (native sliding-window/full attention, #35963); Nemotron 3.5 Lightning spec-dec + NVFP4 (#36186); Nano v3 DFlash/DSpark (#33554); NemotronH Omni Reasoning V3 MTP/vision (#35599); Ling-3.0-flash MXFP4 on GB10 (#36364); DeepSeek-V4-Flash official 0731 checkpoint on MI35x (#36388)
llama.cpp Q2_0 ternary "Bonsai" models on CPU+Metal+CUDA; Apple RDMA RPC transport for multi-Mac; Vulkan fp32-only devices (Haswell hasvk); Hexagon multi-NPU async backend
Ollama Qwen3.8-27B support; Granite 4.1 dense via MLX (#17972); requests open for deepseek-v4-flash:0731 and Q3_K_M MLX Qwen3.8-35B (cloud-only / unshipped)
LiteLLM Bedrock GPT-5.x reasoning_effort mapping fix (#38279); Together Qwen3.7-Max pricing + cache-read cost (#38280); Cerebras full param passthrough (#37674); Vertex AI rerank document text return (#38277)
Unsloth Qwen3.8-27B acknowledgment; Qwen3.5 MTP finetune loss (#6557); EXL3 quantization backend 2/3/4/6/8-bit + MoE (#7115)

Who is ahead: vLLM and SGLang are effectively neck-and-neck on frontier serving architectures, but SGLang showed broader new-model breadth today (5 new architectures) while vLLM prioritized production hardening (MRV2, spec-decode PP). llama.cpp owns the edge/quantized-architecture frontier (ternary Q2_0, Hexagon). LiteLLM tracks models at the pricing/metadata layer, not the kernel layer — which is exactly its lane. Unsloth is the only project adding training-time model support (MTP loss, EXL3 backend) rather than inference-only.

4. Performance Frontier

Optimization effort today clusters in five areas:

  1. Speculative decoding overhead & correctness — vLLM removed DP CPU all-reduce sync from EAGLE/MTP paths (#53694) and generalized adaptive acceptance verification to all draft-model families (#52228); SGLang added spec-dec for Nemotron 3.5 / Nano v3; llama.cpp is fighting an MTP acceptance collapse under parallel slots (#27572) while Ollama reports MTP variants 2× slower on Apple Silicon (#17776). The frontier is no longer "can you spec-decode" but "can you spec-decode under PD, PP, and multi-slot load."

  2. KV cache & long-context serving — SGLang has the most aggressive work: HiCache L3 tiering (with JIT ABI segfault #36302 and storage-key collisions #33268), plus unified_cache gaps at chunked-prefill boundaries (#33714). llama.cpp delivered the biggest raw number: SYCL TILE kernels deliver +42–169% quantized-KV decode on Intel GPUs (#26689). vLLM is restoring prefix-cache hits under MTP (#52244).

  3. Quantization depth — MXFP4+block-FP8 was reverted on H100 (vLLM #53805); SGLang landed AMD MXFP8 MoRI dispatch matching w4a8 MoE input format (#36119); llama.cpp added Q2_0 ternary; Unsloth built an EXL3 fractional-bit backend (#7115). The pattern: quantized MoE is the hardest unsolved correctness surface (see DSV4-Flash EP crashes on Hopper, #35557).

  4. Distributed serving & multi-node — vLLM's MRV2 default rollout (#53183) is the biggest architectural change on the board; SGLang tuned custom all-reduce for sm_107 (#36397); llama.cpp added Apple RDMA as an RPC transport; but distributed is also where the worst breakage lives (vLLM 2-node gloo deadlock, #52907).

  5. Weight loading & serving economics — SGLang's Weight Cache Daemon cut Qwen3-235B FP8 post-quantized load from 306–327s to <1s (#33522); Unsloth added opt-in async_load to avoid proxy timeouts (#7010); Ollama defers eager GPU weight folding to avoid Metal timeouts on slow storage (#17998); LiteLLM moved cost-based routing to break ties on cache-read price (#38164).

5. Layer Positioning

Layer Projects Primary job Today's evidence of positioning
Production serving engines vLLM, SGLang Max throughput/latency for frontier models on multi-GPU; PD disaggregation, spec decode, distributed Both racing on MRV2/PP/PD maturity; both carry the heaviest long-context and distributed bugs
Local / edge runtime llama.cpp, Ollama Run anywhere: quantized, portability, consumer GPUs, Apple Silicon llama.cpp targets ternary Q2_0, Haswell Vulkan, Hexagon NPUs; Ollama handles ollama stop leaks and MLX kernel crashes
LLM gateway / proxy LiteLLM Routing, cost accounting, guardrails, multi-provider abstraction Price corrections, cost-based routing tie-breaks, MCP guardrails, budget-enforcement bugs
Fine-tuning / training framework Unsloth Efficient finetuning + quantized backends + (increasingly) local serving MTP finetune loss, EXL3 backend, MLX context fixes; agent-facing Studio features (auto-compaction, LAN mode)

Notable overlaps: Unsloth is creeping into serving (Studio, LAN access, async load); Ollama and llama.cpp share the same engine core via version bumps; vLLM and SGLang compete directly on nearly every feature (both added new architectures, both have Kimi-K3 problems, both are working PD+spec-decode gaps).

6. Trend Signals

  1. Speculative decoding has crossed the chasm — and correctness is lagging. Every engine now ships or is integrating MTP/EAGLE/DFlash/DSpark variants, but every project also carries an open spec-decode bug: vLLM throughput collapse at batch thresholds (#49548), SGLang DFLASH crashes under PD (#36140), llama.cpp MTP acceptance → 0.0 under parallel slots (#27572), Ollama MTP 2× slower on Mac (#17776). Watch: do not assume spec decode helps until you measure it under your real batch/PD configuration.

  2. Long context is the new production incident class. Kimi-K3 is the canary: engine-wide degeneration after ~240K-token prefill in vLLM (#51039), ~30s load-independent TTFT floor in SGLang (#34815). Watch: add token-diversity health checks, not just liveness probes, to long-context deployments.

  3. Multi-vendor silicon is now a first-class requirement. AMD MI300/MI325 (both engines), Intel SYCL (llama.cpp +42–169% decode), Qualcomm Hexagon NPU, Apple MLX — but each vendor path carries its own crash class (ROCm gfx942 corruption, HIP cross-request leakage on gfx1151, WSL2 IPC crashes). Watch: HPCAAS (high-performance-compute-as-a-service) cost pressures will push more workloads to AMD; gamma-test your exact SKU.

  4. Quantization has no safe defaults. vLLM's Humming revert, Ollama's CUDA 13 sm_86 drop, SGLang's DSV4-Flash MXFP4-on-Hopper crash, and Unsloth's weight-quantized drafter corruption (#51581) all landed in the last 24h. Watch: treat every new quant path as beta until you validate GSM8K-style correctness on your hardware.

  5. Weight loading is becoming an operational discipline. SGLang's Weight Cache Daemon (306s → <1s) and Unsloth's async_load reflect the reality that large models make cold-start and autoscaling costs prohibitive. Watch: cache-daemon-style solutions will appear in vLLM and Ollama within months; plan for shared weight caches in multi-tenant fleets.

  6. Agent tool-calling reliability is still the weakest link across the stack. Evidence: Ollama's Qwen3.8 tool-loop 500s (#17778), DeepSeek-V4 raw DSML token leakage with tool_choice="none" (#35736), Unsloth's enabled_tools no-op on GGUF (#9730), LiteLLM streaming tool_use leakage to Claude Code clients, llama.cpp grammar hyphen-escape fixes. Watch: agent frameworks should validate structured outputs end-to-end per backend, not per model family.

  7. Gateway governance is expanding beyond routing. LiteLLM's Microsoft Agent 365 MCP guardrail with per-user Entra token exchange and Lakera v2 advisory mode signal a shift from "which model" to "what can the model's tools do." Watch: enterprise procurement will increasingly ask for tool-level policy enforcement at the gateway.

Bottom line for technical decision-makers: llama.cpp v0.3.0 is the only clean production checkpoint today; vLLM and SGLang are both mid-migration (MRV2, spec-decode+PD gaps) — pin known-good versions and budget for regression testing. Budget-enforcement false positives (LiteLLM #36926) and scheduler stalls that report healthy (vLLM #53130) mean your observability must validate output quality, not just engine liveness.

Per-Project Reports

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM Digest — 2026-08-26

1. Today's Highlights

No releases shipped in the last 24 hours; the project is consolidating around the Model Runner V2 (MRV2) transition, with a PR to make MRV2 the default for all non-ROCm models (#53183) and two spec-decode optimizations that remove DP synchronization and extend adaptive verification to MTP/EAGLE/DFlash (#53694, #52228). On the stability side, the team reverted MXFP4 + block-FP8 "Humming" support after post-merge H100 correctness failures (#53805), while two high-severity bugs remain open: a scheduler admission stall (#53130) and Kimi-K3 long-context degeneration into repeated tokens (#51039).

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

  • No new releases or version tags in the last 24h.
  • Pending config change: PR #53183 proposes enabling MRV2 for all models by default (ROCm still falls back to MRV1 for some models). Watch for behavior changes when this lands.
  • Reverted feature: PR #53805 reverts the MXFP4 + block-FP8 Humming path (#51332) after exact post-merge H100 evaluation showed invalid outputs on test_gsm8k_correctness. Users on H100 should stay on the standard FP8 path for now.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • K2-Horizon: New model architecture added in PR #53806 (k2_horizon.py, model registry, docs).
  • Idefics3 / SmolVLM: Full ViT encoder CUDA Graph support in PR #47625, precomputing vision position IDs for graph capture.
  • Kimi-K3 on SM100 (B200): PR #53534 enables the low-latency decode GEMM dispatch on SM100 instead of falling back to cuBLAS (currently gated on B300/SM103).
  • EAGLE3-family spec decode with pipeline parallelism: PR #50514 lets eagle3, dflash, and dspark draft models run with PP; draft runs on the last pipeline stage while auxiliary hidden states can come from any stage.
  • ROCm roadmap: Kimi-K3 gfx942/MI325X gap tracking in Issue #52803; Sparse MLA via TRITON_MLA_SPARSE for sm80/120/121 requested in Issue #38006.

4. Performance & Optimization

  • MRV2 default rollout: PR #53183 aims to make MRV2 the default path for all models, with MRV1 retained only for unsupported features.
  • Spec-decode overhead reduction: PR #53694 skips the CPU all-reduce (sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding) before EAGLE/MTP draft prefill and multi-step decode.
  • Adaptive verification generalization: PR #52228 extends acceptance estimation to all draft-model speculators (MTP, EAGLE3, DFlash 1&2), not just DSpark confidence heads.
  • LoRA metadata on CPU: PR #53309 prepares Punica kernel metadata on the CPU with non-blocking H2D copies, reusing prepared metadata for identical mappings.
  • Reported regression: Issue #49548 — dynamic speculative decoding (num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size) on Qwen3.5-122B MTP causes catastrophic aggregate-throughput collapse at the batch-size threshold (the documented PIECEWISE CUDA-graph downgrade costs ~14% single-stream; the multi-stream collapse is the bug).
  • Prefix-cache fix in flight: PR #52244 restores GDN prefix-cache hits under MTP spec decoding (currently prompts with length multiple of the hash unit get zero hits).

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. Scheduler permanently halts admission — Issue #53130: once running + "deferred" requests reach max_num_seqs, the engine stops admitting requests forever, reports healthy, and has mostly free KV cache; only restart recovers. Related fix PR #53799 handles missing req_id in update_from_output (worker OOM path) to avoid an unhandled KeyError.
  2. Kimi-K3 long-context service-wide degeneration — Issue #51039: after a ~240K-token prefill, every subsequent request returns a single repeated degenerate token (NaN logits; packed KDA prefill suspected). Also Issue #51798: Kimi-K3-NVFP4 on 8×B300 produces incoherent reasoning-channel output on v0.27.0.
  3. Multi-node startup deadlock — Issue #52907: 2-node TP-16 DeepSeek-R1 FP8 with Ray executor hangs forever in the gloo barrier inside in_the_same_node_as(), then dies after exactly 30 minutes. Regression between 0.26.1rc1.dev78 and dev148.
  4. MXFP4 + block-FP8 invalid outputs on H100 — reverted in PR #53805 (see Releases).
  5. DeepSeek-V4-Flash silent retrieval corruption on ROCm gfx942 — Issue #52109: prompts ≥ ~4–5K tokens corrupt with the AITER sparse indexer on MI325X.
  6. Decode segfault in P/D disaggregation — Issue #49238: decode instance segfaults on NIXL loadRemoteMD after a prefill pod restart.
  7. Gemma4 fails to start — Issue #51744: vllm/vllm-openai:latest (Transformers 5.15.0) fails to launch Gemma-4-31B QAT NVFP4 (13 👍, open).
  8. Weight-quantized drafter corruption — Issue #51581: DFlash fused-KV projection calls F.linear on a sliced qkv_proj weight, silently corrupting NVFP4/compressed-tensors drafters on DGX Spark.
  9. GLM-5.2 sparse MLA decode gap — Issue #53134: decode is unavailable for GlmMoeDsa on SM90 because the sparse MLA backend lacks decode-LSE support.
  10. Build break on Ampere/Ada — PR #53807 fixes fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp being declared behind the KDA guard instead of the GDN guard.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Pin your images. No release shipped today; latest currently carries the Transformers 5.15.0 / Gemma4 startup break (#51744). Moving to nightly isn't obviously safer given the MRV2-default transition in flight (#53183).
  • Watch long-context and spec-decode deployments. Kimi-K3 at ~240K context can poison a whole engine (#51039); Qwen3.5-122B MTP with dynamic spec decode can collapse throughput at the batch-size threshold (#49548). Add health checks that verify token diversity, not just engine liveness.
  • Heal the scheduler stall with a restart. If an engine reports healthy but stops admitting requests (running + deferred = max_num_seqs), restart rather than scaling (#53130).
  • H100 users: avoid the reverted MXFP4 + block-FP8 Humming path; validate GSM8K-style correctness before adopting new quantization paths (#53805).
  • Tool-calling / structured output fixes are incoming: malformed namespace tools currently return HTTP 500 instead of a validation error (#53763), and reasoning adapters are silently dropped when the reasoning and tool parsers share an engine (#52830).
  • Multimodal pipeline users: modality-scoped mm_processor_kwargs (e.g., videos_kwargs.size) are honored in the token-budget/dummy-input path in PR #53808 — important for Qwen3-VL long-video encoder-cache profiling.
  • New model support to plan for: K2-Horizon (#53806). For multi-node Ray deployments, hold off upgrading until the gloo-barrier deadlock (#52907) is resolved.
SGLang — sgl-project/sglang

SGLang Digest – 2026-08-26

Today’s Highlights

No new release was published in the last 24 hours. The most notable activity surrounds DeepSeek-V4 on AMD (MXFP8 MoRI dispatch, #36119), MiniMax-H3 multi-GPU fixes (#36398), and new model enablement for Spark3 and Nemotron variants (#35963, #36186, #35599). On the reliability side, several high-impact open bugs affect PD-disaggregated deployments, including a ~30s TTFT floor for Kimi-K3 with PP8 (#34815) and DFLASH speculative decoding being unsupported under PD (#36140).

Releases & Breaking Changes

  • None in the last 24 hours. No new versions, API changes, or migration notes to report.

New Model & Hardware Support

  • Spark3 architecture: PR #35963 adds native support with sliding-window/full attention, head-wise attention output gating, TP/PP support — PR #35963
  • Nemotron 3.5 Lightning speculative decoding: PR #36186 adds clean spec-dec support with ModelOpt W4A16 NVFP4 — PR #36186
  • Nano v3 spec-dec + quant recipe: PR #33554 adds DFlash/DSpark support for Nemotron 3.5 — PR #33554
  • NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3: PR #35599 adds architecture recognition so MTP and quantized vision weights load correctly — PR #35599
  • GB10 / DGX Spark: PR #36364 adds Ling-3.0-flash MXFP4 cookbook cells for sm121 — PR #36364
  • AMD MI30x/MI35x CI coverage: PR #36388 moves MI35x DeepSeek-V4-Flash nightly to the official 0731 checkpoint; PR #36396 adds MI30x FP8 accuracy coverage — PR #36388, PR #36396
  • ROCm MLA attention fix: PR #28734 fixes loading/inference of MLA models with Quark PTPC FP8 attention on gfx95 — PR #28734
  • XPU flag removal: PR #34492 removes the SGLANG_USE_SGL_XPU opt-in flag — PR #34492
  • EPD embedding cache: PR #35145 adds L2-only multimodal embedding cache with rank-0 allocation — PR #35145

Performance & Optimization

  • Custom all-reduce v2 for sm_107: PR #36397 tunes the custom all-reduce path for NVIDIA sm_107 — PR #36397
  • AMD DSV4 MXFP8 MoRI dispatch: PR #36119 makes MoRI dispatch match the w4a8 MoE input format, enabling fp8 activations with group-32 e8m0 microscales — PR #36119
  • Simulated expert-choice fusion: PR #29718 fuses simulated expert routing into one Triton kernel, reducing ~5–7 small elementwise ops per layer — PR #29718
  • Diffusion mapped-layer readahead: PR #36323 advises the prefetch kernel ahead of the courier on mapped layers, avoiding slow fault-time readahead on NVMe — PR #36323
  • Weight Cache Daemon: Roadmap issue #33522 reports phase 1 landed; post-quantized weight load on Qwen3-235B FP8 dropped from ~306–327s to <1s — Issue #33522
  • Agentic benchmark dataset: PR #30304 adds --dataset-name agentic to the serving benchmark for long, mostly-cached multi-turn conversations — PR #30304

Stability & Regressions

High-severity or notable issues updated in the last 24h:

  • DeepSeek-V4-Flash EP crashes on Hopper/SM90: PR/issue #35557 fails late during decode CUDA-graph capture because DeepGEMM MXFP4 MegaMoE is SM100-only; error message is misleading — Issue #35557
  • Kimi-K3 PP8 disaggregated prefill has ~30s TTFT floor: Issue #34815 shows a load-independent floor even with PD disaggregation; no fix PR linked — Issue #34815
  • DFLASH spec-dec crashes under PD disaggregation: Issue #36140 reports spec_info None crash and watchdog self-kill when decode side uses --disaggregation-mode decode; DSPARK and EAGLE work — Issue #36140
  • Kimi-K3 crash in v0.5.18: Issue #36018 reports a crash in the release build — Issue #36018
  • DeepSeek-V4 leaks raw DSML tokens: Issue #35736 reports raw DSML leakage even when tool_choice="none" — Issue #35736
  • HiCache L3 segfault on first backup: Issue #36302 is a JIT ABI mismatch in staged_write_back.cuh between nvcc 12.8 compile-time and CUDA 13 runtime cudaMemcpyBatchAsync — Issue #36302
  • WSL2 multimodal crash: Issue #35385 reports scheduler crash because CUDA IPC transport is auto-selected on WSL2, where CUDA IPC is unsupported — Issue #35385
  • MiniMax-M2 CPU inference failure: Issue #35779 reports failure while processing requests on CPU — Issue #35779
  • HiCache storage key collisions: Issue #33268 reports kv_cache_dtype is missing from HiCache storage keys, causing silent cross-run cache collisions — Issue #33268
  • unified_cache skips long prompts: Issue #33714 notes write-through backup is skipped when new-token extend length exceeds chunked_prefill_size — Issue #33714
  • AMD EP8 + FP8 KV cache NCCL error: Issue #29039 (closed/inactive) reports ValueError: Unsupported dtype torch.float8_e4m3fn during CUDA graph capture — Issue #29039

What This Means for Application Developers

  • Be careful with PD + speculative decoding today: DFLASH is not wired into PD disaggregation; use DSPARK or EAGLE for now (#36140).
  • Kimi-K3 PP8 users should measure TTFT before committing: the ~30s floor in disaggregated prefill is load-independent and not yet fixed (#34815).
  • For large-model recovery, the Weight Cache Daemon can reduce weight load from minutes to <1s, which is important for frequent restarts or autoscaling (#33522).
  • DeepSeek-V4 tool-calling deployments should not assume tool_choice="none" fully suppresses DSML control tokens; sanitize outputs or wait for the fix (#35736).
  • Avoid multimodal serving on WSL2 unless the feature transport issue is resolved; the scheduler can crash with no useful hint (#35385).
  • HiCache users should treat cache directories as dtype-sensitive and clear them after changing KV cache dtype or enabling long-prompt workloads (#33268).
llama.cpp — ggml-org/llama.cpp

llama.cpp Digest — 2026-08-26

1. Today's Highlights

llama.cpp officially tagged v0.3.0, with the release train also bringing a reworked KleidiAI build integration, Apple RDMA RPC transport support, and a Metal OOM crash fix. On the performance side, CUDA graphs are now viable on Pascal GPUs (+40% MoE), and SYCL TILE kernels show large quantized-KV decode gains. Several high-severity HIP/Vulkan correctness bugs remain open, including corrupted output on RDNA iGPUs and cross-request response leakage under parallel serving.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

  • v0.3.0 released — version bump and release infrastructure updates (b10621, v0.3.0).
  • KleidiAI build system rework — CMake integration now relies on KleidiAI's own build rules instead of manual kernel listing and -march flags; relevant for ARM CPU builds (b10630, PR #26077).
  • SYCL: tq2_0 marked unsupported — Tensor-quantized 2-bit format disabled on SYCL; check for fallback paths if using this quant type (b10617).
  • CI baseline moved to Ubuntu 24.04 for ROCm builds, matching AMD wheel support (b10629).

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Apple RDMA as RPC transport — allows RPC backends over Apple RDMA, useful for multi-Mac setups (b10628).
  • Q2_0 quantization support for ternary "Bonsai" models across CPU, Metal, and CUDA backends (CPU PR #24448, Metal PR #25419, CUDA PR #25707).
  • Vulkan fp32-only devices — enables Haswell hasvk and similar GPUs lacking fp16/storage-buffer features (PR #27723).
  • CUDA graphs on Pascal (sm_61) — architecture gate relaxed from Volta to DP4A (PR #27721).
  • Hexagon multi-NPU support — async backend overhaul for IQ9/IQ10 class devices (PR #26501).

4. Performance & Optimization

  • CUDA graphs on Pascal: +40% on MoE, +7% on dense models with no regressions (PR #27721).
  • SYCL TILE kernel for quantized KV decode: +42% to +169% across Qwen3.6-35B, Gemma 4 26B/12B at 32K/118K context (PR #26689).
  • MMA FlashAttention for head dim 256 on AMD RDNA: fixes the rocWMMA-removal prompt-processing regression of up to 2x (PR #26419, Issue #26220).
  • Speculative prefill proposed to reduce TTFT via token importance estimation (PR #27692).
  • Scheduler UMA ring buffer plus sanitizer hardening for input tensor handling (PR #27311).
  • Stream MoE routed experts from disk — allows running MoE models larger than RAM with a device-side expert slab cache (PR #25294).

5. Stability & Regressions

  • Cross-request response leakage on integrated HIP GPUs — llama-server with -np 4 --kv-unified can return another request's response verbatim on Strix Halo (gfx1151); high severity (Issue #25992).
  • HIP/ROCm corrupted output on gfx1151 — dense architectures fail with ROCm while Vulkan is correct with byte-identical flags (Issue #27579).
  • MTP draft acceptance collapses to 0.0 under parallel slots — async device→host copy race in self-speculative decoding with -np N (Issue #27572).
  • CUDA kernel stall/watchdog on RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell during execution (Issue #27102).
  • ROCm severe PPL explosion starting at b10040 — reported on Ryzen AI Max+ 395 iGPU (Issue #27506).
  • HIP GDN cache fusion hangs RDNA3 iGPUs — fixed by a PR that disables the fused path on HIP (PR #27722).
  • gpt-oss-20b Harmony channel parsing failures — malformed channel headers fail final PEG parse and error the whole turn (Issue #27720).
  • Metal OOM crash fixed — null-check buffer allocation in Metal backend (b10622).
  • Grammar parser fix — \- escape in character classes now parses correctly, fixing some generated tool-call grammars (b10618).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • v0.3.0 is a good checkpoint for production upgrades, but verify HIP/SYCL paths if you target RDNA iGPUs or Intel GPUs; Vulkan remains the safer fallback on AMD APUs.
  • Parallel serving on HIP iGPUs is risky — cross-request leakage and MTP acceptance bugs are still open; pin -np 1 or use Vulkan when running multi-slot workloads on gfx1151-class hardware.
  • Tool-call reliability improved with the grammar hyphen-escape fix — relevant for agent frameworks using structured outputs with hyphens in schemas.
  • Q2_0 support opens the door for ternary ultra-low-bit models (Bonsai family) on CPU, Metal, and CUDA — useful for edge deployments.
  • CUDA graphs on Pascal extend the performance reach of older data-center and workstation GPUs; expect meaningful gains on MoE models.
  • /v1/models timestamp stability is incoming via PR, which will improve client-side response caching in serving gateways (PR #27719).
Ollama — ollama/ollama

Ollama Digest — 2026-08-26

Today’s Highlights

No new Ollama release landed in the last 24 hours. The project is actively churning on Qwen3.8-era regressions (OpenAI-compatible endpoint hangs, tool-loop failures, MLX/Metal crashes) while merging Claude Desktop integration polish and exposing cached prompt-token metrics. AMD Ryzen NPU support remains the most-voted open feature request.

Releases & Breaking Changes

None in the last 24 hours. Upstream dependency bumps are in review: llama.cpp b10630 (#18003) and MLX version bump (#17955).

New Model & Hardware Support

  • AMD Ryzen NPU support (#5186) — still the top feature request; Linux driver already exists, but no implementation has landed.
  • deepseek-v4-flash:0731 for local users (#17510) — open request; currently cloud-only.
  • Official Q3_K_M MLX quantization for Qwen3.8-35B-A3B (#17869) — requested for 16GB/24GB Apple Silicon Macs.
  • GraniteForCausalLM support in MLX backend (#17972) — adds Granite 4.1 dense model support to mlxrunner.
  • Remove text-only gemma3 MLX model (#18005) — prevents MLX from shadowing the GGUF vision-capable gemma3 path.
  • Upstage Solar Pro 4 request (#17773) — user-requested addition.

Performance & Optimization

  • Report cached prompt tokens (#17943) — adds prompt_eval_cached_count to native responses and cached-token fields to OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs.
  • Cached eval metric in server response (#16916) — broader pass carrying cache_n/MLX cache hits through /api/generate, /api/chat, and compatibility endpoints.
  • Qwen3.8-27B MTP variants measured 2× slower than non-MTP on Apple Silicon (#17776) — reported as potentially expected, but worth measuring before relying on speculative decoding.
  • Avoid Metal GPU timeouts when loading models from slow storage (#17998) — defers eager GPU folding of weights so Metal command buffers do not stall on file reads.

Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. DeepSeek-v4-flash:0731 Cloud infinite thinking loop — Issue #17892 repeated the same reasoning block 221 times over ~1m45s, ended with zero usable output. No fix PR yet.
  2. Qwen3.8 /api/chat tool-loop 500 error — Issue #17778: no user query found in messages during agentic tool-calling. No fix PR yet.
  3. Qwen3.8-27B garbage output on AMD Instinct MI210/ROCm — Issue #17968 is deterministic on 0.32.15; other models work on the same host.
  4. MLX runner crash on Qwen3.8 27B — Issue #17986: Metal kernel v_copyfloat32bfloat16 fails to load. Related work in #17998 targets load-time GPU stalls but not confirmed as a fix for this kernel error.
  5. CUDA 13 silently drops sm_86 support — Issue #17841: RTX 30-series/A40/A6000 fall back to CPU on Ollama 0.32.14 (~7 tok/s, zero GPU allocation). No fix PR yet.
  6. CUDA illegal memory access regression in prefill — Issue #17740 with qwen3.6:35b, prompt-size dependent, introduced between 0.31.2 and 0.32.9.
  7. Typhoon OCR 1.5 3B deterministic @-repetition on RTX 50-series — Issue #17687; works on CPU and other vision models on the same GPU.
  8. Minimax-M3:cloud splits JSON across reasoning/content — Issue #17987: content alone is never valid JSON on /v1/chat/completions.
  9. ollama stop leaks MLX runner on macOS — Issue #17792 has a fix in PR #17798 adding graceful shutdown.
  10. Flux2 Klein image editing broken since ~0.15.6 — Issue #14306 remains open for macOS.

What This Means for Application Developers

  • If you depend on /v1/chat/completions with Qwen3.8 models, validate against this release first. Both hang behavior (#17790) and 500 tool-loop failures (#17778) are live. Native /api/chat may work when the OpenAI-compatible endpoint does not.
  • Tool-calling loops need defensive termination: the no user query found failure mode shows that agentic loops can put the message history into a state the model/server rejects. Treat tool-result message assembly as part of your retry logic.
  • Cached prompt-token reporting is coming in #17943 / #16916. Applications will soon be able to distinguish prefill vs. cache-hit tokens on native, OpenAI-compatible, and Anthropic-compatible paths — useful for cost and latency observability.
  • Cloud reasoning models are not guaranteed to emit valid JSON in message.content — see Minimax-M3 split output (#17987). Concatenate or validate reasoning + content if you require complete structured output.
  • Claude Desktop integration is being actively stabilized — docs in #18004, model-reset behavior in #18000, connection-state UI in #17997, and installed-icon handling in #17995. Routing is still overridable by ~/.claude/settings.json (#17990), so pin environment-based routing explicitly if you rely on ollama launch claude.
LiteLLM — BerriAI/litellm

LiteLLM Digest — 2026-08-26

1. Today's Highlights

No releases shipped in the last 24h, but the project saw heavy PR activity across cost accounting, routing, and guardrails. Key items: Together AI cache-read pricing was fixed (#38280), cost-based routing now breaks ties on cache-read price (#38164), and a new Microsoft Agent 365 MCP guardrail landed (#38241). On the stability front, a fresh Python 3.10 compatibility regression was reported (#38202) alongside the still-open Redis ssl_check_hostname failure (#34614) and false BudgetExceededError under sustained load (#36926).

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

None. No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Fireworks AI Serverless cost entries requested — #37274 (link)
  • novita/openai/gpt-oss-120b pricing entry flagged as incorrect in model_prices_and_context_window.json — #37584 (link)
  • Bedrock GPT-5.x reasoning_effort now mapped to additionalModelRequestFields.reasoning.effort for Converse (previously sent as Anthropic thinking, causing 400s) — PR #38279 (link)
  • Together AI Qwen3.7-Max registry pricing updated to current rates, plus cache_read_input_token_cost added — PR #38280 (link)
  • Bedrock GPT-5.6 long-context pricing fixed; metadata mismatch remains under investigation — #36016 (link, closed)
  • Vertex AI rerank now populates document text in responses when return_documents=true — PR #38277 (link)
  • Cerebras request-parameter passthrough preserved (max_completion_tokens, reasoning, logprobs, service tier, parallel tool calls) — PR #37674 (link)

4. Performance & Optimization

  • Cost-based routing tie-break on cache-read price — cached traffic now picks between equal-priced deployments using cache_read_input_token_cost, eliminating list-order bias — PR #38164 (link)
  • Tag-scoped rate limits (token/request/dollar/concurrency per arbitrary tag value) in progress; native TPM/RPM caps currently only scope to key/user/team — PR #36541 (link)
  • No throughput, latency, or kernel-level work with concrete numbers was reported in this window.

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. Python 3.10 incompatibility — new report aggregating multiple breaking issues for 3.10 environments — #38202 (link, OPEN)
  2. False BudgetExceededError under sustained load — proxy returns 429 near end of ~40-min batch runs with inflated "Current cost"; self-heals in ~2 min; no Redis involved — #36926 (link, OPEN)
  3. Redis failure on v1.93.0 — TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'ssl_check_hostname' breaks cache and budget counters — #34614 (link, OPEN)
  4. Claude models returning sanitized placeholder text — [System: Empty message content sanitised to satisfy protocol] appears as actual output — #24498 (link, OPEN)
  5. OpenAI spec violation in streaming usage chunk — synthetic include_usage event carries non-empty choices instead of choices: [], breaking strict clients — #28735 (link, OPEN)
  6. Masked API keys overwrite real keys — search-tool edit modal pre-fills masked values (e.g. sk****et) and persists them over the real key — #28902 (link, OPEN, security-relevant)
  7. Spend logs miss chained MCP tool calls — only first tool call and first LLM round recorded for streaming /responses with require_approval="never" — #37358 (link, OPEN)
  8. xAI retired Live Search — web_search_options on chat completions now returns HTTP 410; fix PR drops the param — #38278 (link, OPEN)

Closed in last 24h (non-stale, likely fixed): LangSmith tracing 400s (#37269), usage stats breakage on 1.97-RC1 (#36337), anthropic_messages mid-stream fallback (#24004), bedrock_mantle /invoke passthrough (#38054), Responses bridge max_output_tokens truncation (#38088). Note that #22878, #27460, #22173, #12793, and #24583 were closed as stale, not necessarily fixed.

Other notable open fixes in flight: Claude Code streaming tool-call leakage (server-fulfilled headroom_retrieve reaching the client) — PR #36245; Together AI leaking internal thinking_blocks/provider_specific_fields outbound — PR #38275; Together response_format failing open for unregistered models — PR #38269; Fireworks cache_read_input_token_cost not applied in cost calc — #25950.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Budget enforcement can false-positive under sustained load. If you run long batch workloads through the proxy, the ~2-min self-healing 429 behavior (#36926) means you should add retry/backoff, and avoid treating budget_exceeded as a hard terminal state until the budget subsystem is fixed.
  • Pin your Python environment above 3.10 if possible; a fresh compatibility regression report (#38202) suggests 3.10 support is drifting.
  • xAI Live Search is retired. Remove web_search_options from chat completions requests, or upgrade to the fix in #38278 once merged.
  • Fallback visibility is improving. PR #38107 persists attempted_fallbacks and original_model_group into spend-log metadata, which will make it much easier to audit which deployment actually served a request.
  • Guardrail governance is expanding. Expect Microsoft Agent 365 MCP tool-call evaluation (per-user Entra OBO token exchange, #38241) and Lakera v2 skip-message/advisory mode (#34940) in an upcoming release.
  • Anthropic streaming + tool use: if you proxy Claude Code, PR #36245 prevents server-fulfilled retrieval tool calls from being streamed to the client as unusable tool_use blocks — worth tracking for adoption.
Unsloth — unslothai/unsloth

1. Today's Highlights

Two beta releases (v0.1.802/803) shipped with auto-compaction, LAN/remote-access improvements, and important MLX/AMD fixes. For application developers, the most urgent signals are new correctness bugs around tool execution on GGUF models (#9730) and batched vs. single-request greedy generation (#9708), both of which affect agent reliability and evaluation fidelity.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

  • v0.1.803-beta — Bug-fix release with 170+ PRs. Includes MLX/Mac runtime fixes, LAN API keyless/password-less access, keyboard shortcuts, an XET/HTTP download toggle, and an AMD bug fix.
  • v0.1.802-beta — Similar content to .803: MLX fixes, LAN keyless access, XET/HTTP toggle, AMD bug fix, plus auto-compaction support.
  • No explicit breaking API migrations are called out, but the new LAN access mode and download toggle are behavior changes that should be reviewed by operators.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Release notes acknowledge support for Qwen3.8-27B and Unsloth Desktop improvements.
  • PR #7115 — Adds an EXL3 (ExLlamaV3) quantization backend with 2/3/4/6/8-bit and fractional bitrates, plus MoE support (bitsandbytes/transformers 5 gap).
  • PR #8125 — Gives MLX models a real context length propagated from model config to KV cache instead of the hardcoded 4096-token window.
  • PR #9722 — Stops Studio from suggesting bnb-4bit models that MLX cannot load on Mac.
  • PR #6557 — Adds Qwen3.5 MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) finetune loss support.
  • AMD/ROCm: The beta releases include an AMD fix; several AMD-specific issues remain open (see Stability).

4. Performance & Optimization

  • PR #8125 — MLX context length is now model-driven; previously all MLX models ran at a fixed 4096 tokens.
  • PR #7489 — Reuses MLX VLM prompt cache across chat turns, avoiding full multimodal prompt reprocessing.
  • PR #7010 — Adds opt-in async_load for /api/inference/load so large model loads return immediately and run in the background, preventing proxy timeouts.
  • PR #9731 — Behind a flag, maths-bearing markdown blocks are excluded from content-visibility layout/render work.
  • PR #8278 — Fixes packed attention-mask sizing to use padded length rather than token count (training correctness/performance).

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  • Issue #9708 — Batched greedy generation differs from one-at-a-time generation on Qwen3.5-2B and gemma-4-E2B-it after LoRA fine-tuning (left padding). Reproduces on T4. No fix PR yet.
  • Issue #9730 — enabled_tools: ["web_search"] runs no tools at all on local GGUF models; omitting enabled_tools works. Directly impacts agent builds.
  • Issue #9712 — Studio backend stalls for 10–33s on macOS CI before recovering. Not fixed; separate test fix in #9711.
  • Issue #9709 — web_search can be called with an empty object and returns "No query provided", stalling agent turns.
  • Issue #9688 — Repeated SIGKILL recovery replays the same load intent without bound; each replacement process dies and the cycle continues.
  • Issue #9653 — Selecting 256k context loads only 4k on macOS Studio web UI (M3 MBP).
  • Issue #9697 — KV-cache quantization is not reflected in context length when tensor-parallelism is enabled (RTX 5090).
  • Issue #9671 — Auto-compaction triggers at a fixed ~75% of configured context length with no UI control to adjust or disable.
  • Issue #9727 — Image/video generation on AMD GPUs does not work (Studio desktop).
  • Issue #9278 — MiniMax-H3 video generation fails on RX 9070 XT (gfx1201) with hipblasSetStream CUBLAS errors.
  • Issue #9729 — Linux install.sh does not detect AMD GPU under WSL2 unless HSA_ENABLE_DXG_DETECTION=1 is already set.
  • Issue #9482 — New update cannot load model on 16GB RAM integrated GPU; suggests UNSLOTH_ALLOW_HOST_OFFLOAD=1.
  • Issue #7449 — Studio recognizes GPU compute but not VRAM; inference uses system RAM instead.
  • Closed/resolved: #7472 (compaction/rolling context, now implemented), #9398 (HTTP 400 on loaded model), #9551 (AMD VRAM detection after patch) — these are closed, likely fixed or superseded.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Verify tool execution on GGUF backends: The web_search tool behaves inconsistently when enabled_tools is set on local GGUF models (#9730). Add explicit integration tests for your agent toolchains.
  • Batched generation non-determinism is a correctness hazard for offline evaluation and data generation. If you rely on greedy text matching, pin batch size or wait for a fix (#9708).
  • MLX context length is now real: If you deploy on Mac, the hardcoded 4K window disappears with #8125; you can use models at their native context lengths but should update your Studio build.
  • Auto-compaction is here but not yet tunable (#9671). If you need a custom compaction threshold, plan to watch that issue or implement client-side rotation.
  • LAN mode is now keyless/password-less — convenient, but make sure remote networks are trusted or you add your own auth layer.
  • Use async_load (PR #7010) if you load large models behind an HTTP proxy or orchestration layer and hit response-header timeouts.
  • Log/message exports are maturing: PRs #9714 (masked log ZIP export) and #9614 (JSONL message export) are useful for audit trails and training-data pipelines. Note the Docker Hub image is stale (#7999), so pin images carefully.

For all items, see the unslothai/unsloth repository.

item.content:encoded:
AI 官方内容追踪报告 2026-08-26

今日更新 | 新增内容: 27 篇 | 生成时间: 2026-08-26 00:00 UTC

数据来源:

  • Anthropic: anthropic.com — 新增 24 篇（sitemap 共 436 条）
  • OpenAI: openai.com — 新增 3 篇（sitemap 共 922 条）

《AI 官方内容追踪报告》

报告日期：2026-08-26
数据来源：Anthropic（anthropic.com）与 OpenAI（openai.com）官网抓取增量
重要说明：Anthropic 本次抓取到 24 篇页面；OpenAI 仅抓取到 3 条元数据，其中 2 条为同一 URL，且均无正文。本报告对 OpenAI 部分仅客观列举，不做推测性解读。所有标注日期为页面内容原始日期，链接为官网原文。

1. 今日速览

  • Anthropic 今日的增量内容在主题上高度集中：“AI 的经济与劳动力市场影响” 是绝对主线。从 24 篇内容看，Anthropic 正在系统性地发布经济指数报告、国家/地区简报、劳动力市场研究、生产力估算、政策研究基金，以及用户调研结果。
  • 核心亮点之一是 Clio 更名为 “Anthropic Insights”，其隐私保护式真实使用分析工具正在从研究项目向平台化产品演进，也是 Anthropic 一系列经济指数研究的方法论底座。
  • Anthropic 同步强化“政策话语权”布局：宣布 2 亿美元 Economic Futures Research Fund 的研究议程、500 万美元 wellbeing 评测资助计划，并将 Economic Futures Programme 扩展至英国和欧洲。
  • 产品化信号明显：Anthropic Economic Index connector 直接接入 Claude，用户可用自然语言查询 AI 经济数据；Anthropic 还推出了基于 “Anthropic Interviewer” 的月度经济调查。
  • OpenAI 本次数据严重受限，仅能看到标题为 “The Full Stack Behind Abundant Intelligence” 和 “Jalapeno First Results” 的索引页面，无法判断具体内容与战略意图。

2. Anthropic / Claude 内容精选

2.1 news 类（6 篇）

1. Funding better evaluations of AI’s impact on wellbeing

分类：news｜原始日期：2026-08-25
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/news/wellbeing-research-grants

Anthropic 宣布启动 500 万美元资助计划，资助独立研究者开发开源评测，用于衡量 AI 对用户幸福感（wellbeing）的影响。项目强调“独立研究”，提供资金、模型访问和技术支持，成果将开源。
值得注意：Anthropic 承认幸福感是现有评测体系中最难量化的维度，因为需要理解长对话上下文、用户情绪变化和不同情境下的差异。这是一次把“主观福祉”引入 AI 安全评测标准的重要尝试。

2. The Anthropic Economic Index connector

分类：news｜原始日期：2026-07-22
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-economic-index-connector

Anthropic 将 Economic Index 数据做成 Claude 的 connector，用户无需安装，即可在 claude.ai 中直接询问“哪些职业最常用 AI”“科罗拉多人在用 Claude 做什么”等问题。
这是典型的研究数据产品化动作：把原本给学者/记者/政策制定者用的经济指数，变成普通用户可对话查询的公共资源。它同时也在增强 Claude 的“数据问答”场景。

3. Supporting ambitious external research through the Anthropic Economic Futures Research Fund

分类：news｜原始日期：2026-07-22
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/news/economic-futures-research-fund-agenda

Anthropic 公布了 Economic Futures Research Fund 的研究议程，总额 2 亿美元，鼓励外部研究者申请。重点覆盖五个领域：企业/工作场所层面的 AI 影响、AI 转型中的就业支持、收入支持体系现代化、让工人分享 AI 增长红利、公共投资证据研究。
这不仅是学术资助，更像在构建“AI 劳动力政策”的思想基础设施。Anthropic 试图在政策工具尚未成型前，抢先定义哪些干预措施值得被研究和试行。

4. Launching the Anthropic Economic Futures Programme in the UK and Europe

分类：news｜原始日期：2025-11-05
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/news/economic-futures-uk-europe

Anthropic 将 Economic Futures Programme 从美国扩展到英国和欧洲，并与伦敦政治经济学院（LSE）合办研讨会；为英欧研究者提供研究资助和 Claude credits。
一个有趣的细节是：英国用户使用 Claude 最常见的场景是学术研究、写作和教育内容，而非编程。这为区域 AI 政策提供了不同视角。

5. Anthropic Economic Index: Insights from Claude 3.7 Sonnet

分类：news｜原始日期：2025-03-27
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-economic-index-insights-from-claude-sonnet-3-7

这是 Economic Index 的第二份研究，围绕 Claude 3.7 Sonnet 推出后的真实使用数据。核心发现包括：编程、教育、科学和医疗健康使用份额上升；用户更倾向于用“extended thinking”模式完成计算机科学、软件开发、多媒体动画等任务。
报告还首次公开了任务级和职业级的增强/自动化拆分，例如编辑和撰稿任务更多是“人机协作”，而翻译和口译任务更多是“指令式自动化”。

6. Introducing the Anthropic Economic Index

分类：news｜原始日期：2025-02-10
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/news/the-anthropic-economic-index

Anthropic 宣布启动 Economic Index，这是其理解 AI 对劳动市场与经济影响的长期项目。首份报告基于数百万条匿名 Claude.ai 对话，并开放数据集供研究者使用。
关键数据：约 36% 的职业在至少四分之一的任务中使用 AI；约 4% 的职业在四分之三的任务中使用 AI；AI 使用偏向“增强”（57%）而非“自动化”（43%）。这是 Anthropic 试图为“AI 如何改变工作”提供经验证据的起点。

2.2 research 类（18 篇）

A. 经济指数核心报告与方法论

7. Clio: Privacy-preserving insights into real-world AI use

分类：research｜原始日期：2024-12-12，2026-08-24 更新
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/clio

Clio 是 Anthropic 开发的隐私保护型真实 AI 使用分析系统，能够在不暴露个人隐私的前提下，对 Claude.ai 上的海量对话进行聚类和洞察，类似“AI 版 Google Trends”。
页面更新显示，这一系统现已更名为 Anthropic Insights。这意味着原本偏研究性质的 Clio，正在变成可持续对外输出 AI 社会观察的正式平台。它也是 Economic Index 和多项调查的方法论基石。

8. Anthropic Economic Index report: Economic primitives

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-01-15
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/anthropic-economic-index-january-2026-report

这份报告第一次提出“economic primitives”概念，用五个基础维度度量 AI 使用的经济含义：用户和 AI 技能、任务复杂度、AI 自主性、任务成功率、用途（工作/教育/个人）。数据抽样自 2025 年 11 月，即 Opus 4.5 发布前。
报告发现显著的地理差异，并提供了迄今最全面的多维数据集。其价值在于：不只是看“ChatGPT 在哪些行业被用”，而是衡量 AI 使用的方式、深度和结果。

9. The Anthropic Economic Index report: New building blocks for understanding AI use

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-01-15
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/economic-index-primitives

该页面是上一条“Economic primitives”报告面向公众的入口/摘要版，核心内容与 /research/anthropic-economic-index-january-2026-report 高度重叠。
在本次抓取中两个 URL 同时出现，可能是同一研究的不同发布通道。此处作为独立 URL 记录，但读者可选择其中一版详细阅读。

10. Anthropic Economic Index report: Uneven geographic and enterprise AI adoption

分类：research｜原始日期：2025-09-15
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/anthropic-economic-index-september-2025-report

报告用历史技术扩散对比凸显 AI 的“史无前例”速度：美国员工使用 AI 的比例从 2023 年的 20% 增至 2025 年的 40%；相比之下，电力、PC、互联网的普及耗时更长。
但作者指出：AI 在企业端的扩散并不均匀，尤其是企业从“窄任务”到“通用任务”的采用模式，决定了 AI 经济价值的释放节奏。

11. Anthropic Economic Index: Tracking AI’s role in the US and global economy

分类：research｜原始日期：2025-09-15
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/economic-index-geography

Economic Index 第三份报告，首次提供美国各州和全球多个国家的 Claude 使用画像。例如马萨诸塞州最“过度代表”的使用是科研，夏威夷是旅行规划，巴西用户使用翻译和语言学习的频率是全球平均的 6 倍。
全球来看，软件工程仍是几乎所有地区最大的使用类别，但区域产业结构会显著影响 AI 的具体用途。

12. Anthropic Economic Index report: Cadences

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-06-26
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/economic-index-june-2026-report

这份报告是一次重要的方法论升级：Anthropic 明确表示，由于 Claude Code 和 Cowork 的快速增长，AI 使用已从“对话”转向“长时间 agentic 任务”，聊天记录不再能完全捕捉 AI 的真实经济影响。
因此，他们重构了数据管道：更高频抽样到小时级、引入输出分类器、区分 chat/Cowork/1P API。这意味着 Anthropic 正在为“Agentic AI 时代”重新定义经济统计口径。

13. Anthropic Economic Index report: Learning curves

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-03-24
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/economic-index-march-2026-report

报告基于 2026 年 2 月数据，覆盖 Opus 4.5 发布三个月后、Opus 4.6 发布期间的变化。结果显示：增强型使用比例上升；Claude.ai 端 top10 任务集中度下降，说明使用场景更分散。
更核心的发现是“学习曲线”：高资历用户通过积累习惯和策略，能更高效地利用 Claude。这暗示 AI 收益可能向“更会用 AI 的人”倾斜，而不是平均分布。

B. 用户调查与国家/地区简报

14. What 81,000 people told us about the economics of AI

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-04-22
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/81k-economics

基于 81,000 名 Claude 用户的开放性问题调查，将用户主观感受与 Economic Index 的用量数据对接。结果显示：AI 暴露程度更高的职业更担心失业；早期职业者更焦虑；收入最高和最低的人群报告了最大的生产力提升。
一个反直觉的发现是：体验过最大“加速感”的人，反而对失业更担忧。这为“AI 提高生产力但不一定降低焦虑”提供了证据。

15. Announcing the Anthropic Economic Index Survey

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-04-22
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/economic-index-survey-announcement

Anthropic 宣布启动月度 Economic Index Survey，通过自有工具 Anthropic Interviewer 收集 Claude 用户的主观经历和预期。
这相当于在客观使用数据之外增加了一条“实时感受”管道，弥补传统劳动市场指标滞后的问题。调查结果将成为 Anthropic 经济研究的重要数据来源。

16. How Australia Uses Claude: Findings from the Anthropic Economic Index

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-03-31
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/how-australia-uses-claude

澳大利亚占全球 Claude.ai 流量的 1.6%，人均使用量是人口规模的 4 倍以上；新南威尔士州和维多利亚州合计占全国对话的 68%。
与其他国家相比，澳大利亚的用途更多元：编程占比低于全球基线 8 个百分点，办公、销售、管理和个人生活任务更多。该报告发布时 Anthropic 正宣布在悉尼设办公室并与澳政府签署 AI 安全合作 MOU。

17. How Canada uses Claude: Findings from the Anthropic Economic Index

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-07-14
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/how-canada-uses-claude

加拿大占全球 Claude.ai 流量 2.6%，总量排第 8；人均使用量是预期的 4 倍，在美国之外的主要国家中最高。安大略省占 43.9% 的对话，BC 省人均使用最高。
研究进一步发现，省份间的采用差异更多由产业结构而非收入解释：专业、科学和技术服务业占比高的省份使用量更大。

18. India Country Brief: The Anthropic Economic Index

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-02-16
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/india-brief-economic-index

印度占全球 Claude.ai 使用量的 5.8%，位列第二，仅次美国；但人均使用量在 116 个国家和地区中排第 101。
印度用户的特点是：更多用于职业场景、赋予 AI 更高自主性、任务更复杂且耗时更长。Anthropic 认为印度用户已经走在“使用 AI 的边界”。

C. 劳动力市场、生产力与政策研究

19. Labor market impacts of AI: A new measure and early evidence

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-03-05
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/labor-market-impacts

Anthropic 提出一个新指标“observed exposure”，结合理论上的 LLM 能力和真实使用数据，并对“自动化型”和工作相关使用赋权。研究发现：AI 实际能力离理论覆盖还有很大距离；高暴露职业预计未来增长更慢；这些职业的从业者更可能是年长、女性、高学历、高收入。
与直觉相反，自 2022 年底以来，并未观察到高暴露职业系统性失业上升，但年轻人在高暴露职业中的招聘确有放缓。该指标可能成为未来 AI 就业风险评估的基准。

20. How well do job retraining programs work?

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-08-12
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/reviewing-the-evidence-on-worker-retraining-programs

Anthropic 与独立研究员 David Roodman 合作，对 56 项美国随机实验进行元分析，并参考欧洲实验证据，系统评估“再就业培训”的效果。
结论是温和正面但有限：培训使就业率提高 2~3 个百分点，年收入增加约 1,000 美元，单人成本约 13,000 美元；政府通过税收和减少福利支出可收回一半以上成本。该报告直接为 AI 时代的劳动力政策提供了成本效益数据库。

21. Estimating AI productivity gains from Claude conversations

分类：research｜原始日期：2025-11-25
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/estimating-productivity-gains

Anthropic 抽样 10 万条真实 Claude.ai 对话，估算任务在无 AI 与有 AI 情况下所需时间。结论是：这些任务人工平均约 90 分钟，Claude 将单任务速度提升约 80%。
推而广之，当前一代 AI 模型可能为美国未来十年劳动生产率的年增长贡献约 1.8%——约为近年增速的 2 倍。报告也承认未计算人类验证质量的时间，因此存在高估风险。

D. Agent 使用与编程

22. How Claude Code is used in practice

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-06-16
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/claude-code-expertise

该研究基于 40 万个 Claude Code 会话，揭示了 agentic coding 的真实协作模式：人类主要负责“做什么”的规划，Claude 主要负责“怎么做”的执行；用户领域专长越强，Claude 单条指令能完成的活越多。
另一个关键趋势：七个月内调试耗时占比下降近一半，使用转向部署、数据分析和非代码文档撰写等更端到端的 agentic 任务；典型任务价值平均上升约 25%。

23. Coding agents in the social sciences

分类：research｜原始日期：2026-05-27
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/coding-agents-social-sciences

对 1,260 名社会科学家的调查显示：81% 尝试过在研究中用 AI 聊天机器人，但只有 20% 真正采用了编程 agent（如 Claude Code）。
使用率存在显著不平等：常见男性名字的研究者使用 coding agent 的比例是常见女性名字研究者的 2 倍；顶尖大学研究者使用率比其他人高 40%。用户确实发布更多工作论文和基金申请，但作者谨慎表示可能只是早期采用者的既有优势。

24. Anthropic Economic Index: AI’s impact on software development

分类：research｜原始日期：2025-04-28
链接：https://www.anthropic.com/research/impact-software-development

基于 50 万条编程相关交互，比较 Claude.ai 和 Claude Code 的自动化差异。结果显示：Claude Code 会话中 79% 属于自动化，而 Claude.ai 只有 49%。
这说明“编程 agent”与普通对话助手在劳动替代模式上有本质不同。软件开发者、企业技术决策者需要重新评估“AI 编码”究竟是增强还是自动化。

4. 战略信号解读

4.1 Anthropic 正在构建“AI 经济影响”的标准话语权

Anthropic 这次集中释放的内容，几乎可以看作一份完整的政策研究组合包：

  • 它用 Economic Index 提供“AI 正在干什么”的量化事实；
  • 用 81,000 人调查和月度 Survey 提供“人类感受如何”的主观数据；
  • 用 labor market impacts 和 retraining 报告评估“干预政策是否有效”；
  • 用 2 亿美元研究基金和 wellbeing 资助计划，引导学术资源进入自己的研究方向。

这已经不是简单的企业社会责任（CSR），而是一种 “研究型政策影响”策略：在监管者还没有形成标准之前，Anthropic 想成为那个定义“AI 对劳动市场影响如何衡量”的机构。这也可能成为其与 OpenAI 等竞争对手差异化的重要资产。

4.2 技术优先级：从对话走向 Agent，从使用度量走向结果度量

Anthropic 在 Cadences 报告中说得很清楚：“聊天记录不再能完全捕捉人们如何使用 AI。”随着 Claude Code、Cowork 等 agent 产品的增长，AI 使用形态已经从“人问 AI 答”变成“人委托 AI 执行多步任务”。

这带来两个信号：

  • 产品层面：Anthropic 会继续押注 agentic coding 和 agentic work，而不仅仅是聊天助手；
  • 研究层面：传统的“任务分类 + 职业对照”分析方法正在被升级为更复杂的“自主性、成功率、学习曲线”等新维度。

4.3 竞争态势：Anthropic 在议题设置上领先，但 OpenAI 数据缺位

本次抓取中，Anthropic 完全主导了“AI 经济影响”议题，而 OpenAI 近乎失语。由于缺少 OpenAI 正文，不能判断其是否在跟进同类研究。但从标题来看，OpenAI 关注的可能是“abundant intelligence”（大规模智能供给）和某个疑似代号 “Jalapeno” 的研究结果，方向更偏技术/基础设施。

如果这种差异是持续的，那么两家公司的战略叙事将出现明显分化：

  • Anthropic：强调“负责任地理解 AI 的社会经济影响”；
  • OpenAI：可能更强调“让智能变得丰富、便宜、可规模获取”。

4.4 对开发者和企业用户的潜在影响

  • 企业用户：Anthropic Economic Index connector 可以直接回答“同行在用什么 AI 做哪些任务”这类问题，有助于做竞品分析和工作流设计。
  • HR / 劳动力规划：“observed exposure” 和 retraining 报告提供了新工具，企业可以评估内部岗位的 AI 暴露风险，提前规划培训或转岗。
  • 开发者：Claude Code 的数据证明 agentic coding 正在增加，且调试时间大幅下降。开发工具链和团队工作流程应尽快适配“人规划、AI 执行”的新模式。
  • 政策合规：Anthropic 正在通过研究资助和数据开放，把“AI 经济影响”的话语权握在手中。企业如果依赖政府补贴或公共政策，需要关注这些指标对未来监管方向的影响。

5. 值得关注的细节

  1. “Clio” 改名 “Anthropic Insights”
    这是从“研究工具”到“公共产品”的标志性变化。未来 Anthropic 可能会持续以 Insights 品牌发布 AI 社会影响、经济影响报告，形成固定 IP。

  2. “Cowork” 这一产品名出现
    在 Cadences 报告中，Anthropic 将 Claude Code 与 Cowork 并列，说明其内部已经将“协作型 agent 工作”视为正式产品品类。这是继 Claude Code 之后，值得追踪的下一个产品线。

  3. “Jalapeno” 首次出现
    OpenAI 的标题 “Jalapeno First Results” 中，“Jalapeno” 是一个此前未见于本次抓取的代号。虽然无正文，但通常这种命名风格可能指向模型或研究项目；建议下次抓取优先关注。

  4. “Economic primitives” 和 “observed exposure” 是新造概念
    Anthropic 正在有意创造一套可复用的指标语言。这些概念未来可能被学术界、政策界引用，甚至成为行业默认标准。对研究者和分析师来说，理解这些新指标比看单篇报告更重要。

  5. 密集发布背后的“政策日程”暗示
    虽然部分条目是历史内容，但 Anthropic 在 2026 年 7-8 月密集更新了 Economic Futures Research Fund、wellbeing grants、retraining review、Canada brief 等页面。这些内容共同构成一份“AI 劳动力政策白皮书”，很可能是在为某个政策倡导节点做铺垫。

  6. “隐私保护”贯穿所有研究
    从 Clio 到 Economic Index，再到各国家简报，Anthropic 都在强调“隐私保护式分析”。这既可以降低用户隐私风险，也是向监管者释放“我们做事合规”的信号。随着欧英监管趋严，这种公开承诺会增加企业信任度。

报告完。

下次追踪建议：

  • 优先补充 OpenAI 缺失的正文，尤其是 “Jalapeno” 的后续发布；
  • 持续跟踪 Anthropic Economic Index connector 的功能迭代；
  • 关注 Anthropic 是否会将 Insights 从研究品牌升级为独立产品线；
  • 留意 “Cowork” 产品正式发布的时间节点。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。
